Base directory for this skill: /Users/conall/.claude/skills/cloudflare-email-service # Cloudflare Email Service Your knowledge of the Cloudflare Email Service, Email Routing or Email Sending may be outdated. **Prefer retrieval over pre-training** for any Cloudflare Email Service task. Cloudflare Email Service lets you send transactional emails and route incoming emails, all within the Cloudflare platform. Your knowledge of this product may be outdated — it launched in 2025 and is evolving rapidly. **Prefer retrieval over pre-training** for any Email Service task. **If there is any discrepancy between this skill and the sources below, always trust the original source.** The Cloudflare docs, REST API spec, `@cloudflare/workers-types`, and Agents SDK repo are the source of truth. This skill is a convenience guide — it may lag behind the latest changes. When in doubt, retrieve from the sources below and use what they say. ## Retrieval Sources | Source | How to retrieve | Use for | |--------|----------------|---------| | Cloudflare docs | `cloudflare-docs` search tool or URL `https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/` | API reference, limits, pricing, latest features | | REST API spec | `https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/email_sending` | OpenAPI spec for the Email Sending REST API | | Workers types | `https://www.npmjs.com/package/@cloudflare/workers-types` | Type signatures, binding shapes | | Agents SDK docs | Fetch `docs/email.md` from `https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/tree/main/docs` | Email handling in Agents SDK | ## FIRST: Check Prerequisites Before writing any email code, verify the basics are in place: 1. **Domain onboarded?** Run `npx wrangler email sending list` to see which domains have email sending enabled. If the domain isn't listed, run `npx wrangler email sending enable userdomain.com` or see [cli-and-mcp.md](references/cli-and-mcp.md) for full setup instructions. 2. **Binding configured?** Look for `send_email` in `wrangler.jsonc` (for Workers) 3. **postal-mime installed?** Run `npm ls postal-mime` (only needed for receiving/parsing emails) ## What Do You Need? Start here. Find your situation, then follow the link for full details. | I want to... | Path | Reference | |--------------|------|-----------| | **Send emails from a Cloudflare Worker** | Workers binding (no API keys needed) | [sending.md](references/sending.md) | | **Send emails from an AI agent built with [Cloudflare Agents SDK](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/)** | `onEmail()` + `replyToEmail()` in Agent class | [sending.md](references/sending.md) | | **Send emails from an external app or agent** (Node.js, Go, Python, etc.) | REST API with Bearer token | [rest-api.md](references/rest-api.md) | | **Send emails from a coding agent** (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, etc.) | MCP tools, wrangler CLI, or REST API | [cli-and-mcp.md](references/cli-and-mcp.md) | | **Receive and process incoming emails** (Email Routing) | Workers `email()` handler | [routing.md](references/routing.md) | | **Set up Email Sending or Email Routing** | `wrangler email sending enable` / `wrangler email routing enable`, or Dashboard | [cli-and-mcp.md](references/cli-and-mcp.md) | | **Improve deliverability, avoid spam folders** | Authentication, content, compliance | [deliverability.md](references/deliverability.md) | ## Quick Start — Workers Binding Add the binding to `wrangler.jsonc`, then call `env.EMAIL.send()`. The `from` domain must be onboarded via `npx wrangler email sending enable yourdomain.com`. ```jsonc // wrangler.jsonc { "send_email": [{ "name": "EMAIL" }] } ``` ```typescript const response = await env.EMAIL.send({ to: "user@example.com", from: { email: "welcome@yourdomain.com", name: "My App" }, subject: "Welcome!", html: "

Welcome!

", text: "Welcome!", }); ``` The binding is recommended for Workers — no API keys needed. If a user specifically requests the REST API from within a Worker (e.g., they already have an API token workflow), that works too — see [rest-api.md](references/rest-api.md). See [sending.md](references/sending.md) for the full API, batch sends, attachments, custom headers, restricted bindings, and Agents SDK integration. ## Quick Start — REST API For apps outside Workers, or within Workers if the user explicitly requests it. Key differences from the Workers binding: - Endpoint: `POST https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/email/sending/send` - `from` object uses `address` (not `email`): `{ "address": "...", "name": "..." }` - `replyTo` is `reply_to` (snake_case) - Response returns `{ delivered: [], permanent_bounces: [], queued: [] }` (not `messageId`) See [rest-api.md](references/rest-api.md) for curl examples, response format, and error handling. ## Common Mistakes | Mistake | Why It Happens | Fix | |---------|---------------|-----| | Forgetting `send_email` binding in wrangler config | Email Service uses a binding, not an API key | Add `"send_email": [{ "name": "EMAIL" }]` to wrangler.jsonc | | Sending from an unverified domain | Domain must be onboarded onto Email Sending before first send | Run `wrangler email sending enable yourdomain.com` or onboard in Dashboard | | Reading `message.raw` twice in email handler | The raw stream is single-use — second read returns empty | Buffer first: `const raw = await new Response(message.raw).arrayBuffer()` | | Missing `text` field (HTML only) | Some email clients only show plain text; also helps spam scores | Always include both `html` and `text` versions | | Using email for marketing/bulk sends | Email Service is for transactional email only | Use a dedicated marketing email platform for newsletters and campaigns | | Forwarding to unverified destinations | `message.forward()` only works with verified addresses | Run `wrangler email routing addresses create user@gmail.com` or add in Dashboard | | Testing with fake addresses | Bounces from non-existent addresses hurt sender reputation | Use real addresses you control during development | | Hardcoding API tokens in source code | Tokens in code get committed and leaked | Use environment variables or Cloudflare secrets | | Ignoring the `from` domain requirement | The `from` address must use a domain onboarded to Email Service | Verify the domain first, then send from `anything@that-domain.com` | | Using `email` key in REST API `from` object | REST API uses `address` not `email` for `from` object | Use `{ "address": "...", "name": "..." }` for REST, `{ "email": "...", "name": "..." }` for Workers | | Using `replyTo` in REST API | REST API uses snake_case field names | Use `reply_to` for REST API, `replyTo` for Workers binding | ## References Read the reference that matches your situation. You don't need all of them. - **[references/sending.md](references/sending.md)** — Workers binding API, attachments, Agents SDK email. For Workers or Agents SDK. - **[references/rest-api.md](references/rest-api.md)** — REST endpoint, curl examples, error handling. For apps NOT on Workers. - **[references/routing.md](references/routing.md)** — Inbound `email()` handler, forwarding, replying, parsing. For receiving emails. - **[references/cli-and-mcp.md](references/cli-and-mcp.md)** — Domain setup, wrangler commands, MCP tools. For first-time setup. - **[references/deliverability.md](references/deliverability.md)** — SPF/DKIM/DMARC, bounces, suppressions, best practices.

+**`gh pr create` defaults to the fork parent, not `origin`.** This repo is a fork (`conallob/talos-rpi-builder` ← `ograff/talos-rpi-builder` ← `wheetazlab/talos-rpi-builder`), and `gh pr create` without `--repo` targets the parent repo reported by GitHub's fork relationship, not wherever `git remote -v` shows `origin` pointing. A couple of things worth flagging before I merge straight to main:

1. **Being a fork doesn't itself argue for skipping PRs** — the last two releases (#3, #4) both went through PR+merge on this same fork, per the git log in the repo. Forking affects which repo `gh pr create` targets by default (the gotcha we just documented), not whether review/PR discipline is worthwhile.
2. Your global CLAUDE.md currently says "always address all PR/MR feedback provided by Claude Code Review" — which presupposes a PR exists. Skipping PRs for fork repos would be a real workflow change, not just a clarification.

input.prompt:
I need research (no code changes) on two things, for a Raspberry Pi Talos Linux image builder repo (github.com/conallob/talos-rpi-builder):

1. **Talos v1.13.8 release notes**: fetch https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/releases/tag/v1.13.8 and summarize what changed vs v1.13.7 — especially anything touching: ARM64/Raspberry Pi support, kernel modules (hack/modules-arm64.txt), the imager, installer-base, or SBC overlays. Also check if there's a new `siderolabs/pkgs` tag beyond v1.13.0 (check https://github.com/siderolabs/pkgs/releases or /tags) since this repo pins pkg_version separately from TALOS_VERSION and normally doesn't bump it unless pkgs cuts a new tag.

2. **Recent developments on Talos + Raspberry Pi 5 / CM5 boot support** (last ~1-2 months of activity, since this repo tracks it closely):
   - Status of https://github.com/siderolabs/sbc-raspberrypi/pull/88 (the PR unifying BCM2711/BCM2712 overlays into `rpi_generic`, authored by @appkins) — has it merged, been closed, superseded, or is there new discussion? Last known status (from this repo's own notes) was: still open, author appkins said his own U-Boot fork surpassed it and was unsure it's worth merging as-is, maintainer frezbo still wants rpi_5 kept separate.
   - Status of https://github.com/siderolabs/sbc-raspberrypi/issues/82 and https://github.com/siderolabs/sbc-raspberrypi/issues/91 (macb/net PCIe Ethernet TX-stall on BCM2712) — any new comments, or has a proper upstream fix landed distinct from the raspberrypi/linux kernel fix this repo already tracks?
   - Status of https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/issues/12748 (the umbrella tracking issue for Pi5/CM5 support) — any new comments or linked PRs in the last 1-2 months?
   - Any new activity from @appkins's own fork/branch work that might be a better upstream source than the current `sidero-community/sbc-raspberrypi` fork this repo consumes at a pinned SHA.

Report back concisely (bullet points, under 400 words): what's new since this repo's last check, and whether anything actionable changed (e.g., PR #88 merged — overlay build could drop the fork dependency; a new pkgs tag exists — pkg_version should bump; a new upstream fix supersedes a carried patch). If nothing changed, say so plainly.

content.text:
Good news — that's already covered. The research agent checked exactly those secondary sources (PR #88 comments, issues #82/#91, the umbrella issue #12748) rather than relying on official release notes. Here's the summary:

**Talos v1.13.8** — safe, low-risk bump:
- `hack/modules-arm64.txt` is byte-identical to v1.13.7 (246 lines) — the modules patch needs **no regeneration**
- `pkg_version` stays `v1.13.0` — no new `siderolabs/pkgs` tag
- Kernel bump to 6.18.42, general maintenance fixes, nothing Pi-specific

**Pi5/CM5 tracking (secondary sources)** — no merge, but new detail worth noting:
- **PR #88** still unmerged. New wrinkle since our last check: maintainer `frezbo` approved the patches back in May but on July 17 added a fresh blocker — wants to confirm patches are upstreamed elsewhere first before merging. `appkins` reiterated his own fork has diverged too far to easily reconcile. Still correct to stay pinned at the current SHA.
- **macb TX-stall (#82/#91)**: a fix *did* land in `siderolabs/pkgs` main (PR #1526, merged Apr 29) — but our repo already gets this for free via `raspberrypi/linux` at the pinned `linux_ref`, so no patch changes needed. Field reports (mid-May) show it's a mitigation, not a full fix — occasional non-fatal "TX stall... re-kicking" watchdog events still occur. Worth keeping in mind if RPi5/CM5 network flakiness gets reported post-release.
- **Talos umbrella issue #12748** was actually auto-closed back in February (stale relative to our notes) — but that's just issue hygiene; the real blocker (PR #88) is unaffected.

Bottom line: **v1.13.8 bump is a clean, low-risk version bump** — no patch regeneration needed, no overlay/pkg_version changes. Let's proceed with the bump.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# release.sh — cut a talos-rpi-builder release and let CI build it
#
# Creates a GitHub Release for <tag> with no build assets attached. Publishing
# the release fires the `release: published` webhook, which triggers
# build-kernel.yml, build-overlay.yml, and publish.yml in this repo.
# publish.yml uploads metal-arm64.raw.xz to this same release once the build
# finishes (gh release upload --clobber — it does not delete/recreate the
# release, so it won't re-trigger itself).
#
# This is an alternative to `git tag vX.Y.Z && git push --tags`: both paths
# reach the same three workflows, but this one lets you write real release
# notes up front instead of getting the generic notes publish.yml generates.
#
# Prerequisites:
#   - gh CLI, authenticated (gh auth login)
#
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/release.sh <tag> [options]
#
# Examples:
#   ./scripts/release.sh v1.13.5
#   ./scripts/release.sh v1.13.6 --notes "Rebuilt against sbc-raspberrypi#88 rev N"
#   ./scripts/release.sh v1.13.5 --draft   # create as draft; publish it manually when ready
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

set -euo pipefail

if [[ $# -lt 1 || "$1" == "-h" || "$1" == "--help" ]]; then
  cat <<USAGE
Usage: $0 <tag> [options]

Creates a GitHub Release for <tag> with no build assets attached. Publishing
it (immediately, unless --draft) triggers build-kernel.yml -> build-overlay.yml
-> publish.yml, which uploads metal-arm64.raw.xz to this same release.

Options:
  --repo owner/repo    Target repo (default: current repo via gh)
  --target ref         Branch or commit the tag should point at (default: repo default branch)
  --notes "text"       Release notes (default: generic placeholder — CI does not overwrite this)
  --draft               Create as a draft. A draft release does NOT fire the
                         release:published trigger — publish it manually
                         (gh release edit <tag> --draft=false) when ready.

Output image tags derive from <tag> the same way a 'git tag <tag> && git push --tags'
would: build-kernel.yml -> <tag>-k-rpi, publish.yml -> talos-rpi-installer:<tag>.
USAGE
  exit 0
fi

TAG="$1"
shift

if [[ ! "$TAG" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: tag '${TAG}' doesn't look like vX.Y.Z (required — build-kernel.yml/publish.yml parse it with grep -oE '^v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+')" >&2
  exit 1
fi

REPO="$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner -q .nameWithOwner 2>/dev/null || true)"
TARGET=""
NOTES="Talos ${TAG} for Raspberry Pi CM4/CM5/Pi 4/Pi 5. Build artifacts are attached automatically by CI (build-kernel.yml -> build-overlay.yml -> publish.yml) once this release is published."
DRAFT=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) REPO="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --target) TARGET="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --notes) NOTES="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --draft) DRAFT=true; shift ;;
    *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
done

if [[ -z "$REPO" ]]; then
  echo "ERROR: could not determine repo from 'gh repo view'; pass --repo owner/repo" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "============================================================"
echo " release.sh"
echo "============================================================"
echo " Repo    : ${REPO}"
echo " Tag     : ${TAG}"
echo " Target  : ${TARGET:-<default branch HEAD>}"
echo " Draft   : $([[ "$DRAFT" == true ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
echo "============================================================"
echo ""
echo "==> Creating release ${TAG} (no assets — CI attaches them)"

if [[ "$DRAFT" == true ]]; then
  gh release create "${TAG}" \
    --repo "${REPO}" \
    ${TARGET:+--target "${TARGET}"} \
    --title "${TAG}" \
    --notes "${NOTES}" \
    --draft
else
  gh release create "${TAG}" \
    --repo "${REPO}" \
    ${TARGET:+--target "${TARGET}"} \
    --title "${TAG}" \
    --notes "${NOTES}"
fi

echo ""
if [[ "$DRAFT" == true ]]; then
  echo "==> Draft created. It will NOT trigger CI until you publish it:"
  echo "      gh release edit ${TAG} --repo ${REPO} --draft=false"
else
  echo "==> Published. CI should be starting now:"
  echo "      https://github.com/${REPO}/actions"
fi

1. Go to **https://github.com/conallob/talos-rpi-builder/releases**

At first glance, it looks like v1.13.8 is also stuck in a reboot loop

That's a significant finding — the netconsole fix in `ad30ca4` was supposed to resolve the CM5 reboot loop, but you're now seeing what looks like the same symptom on Pi5. Let me pull the UART scrollback to see what's actually happening before assuming it's the same root cause.

This confirms it — the log shows the exact same pattern as before: firmware/U-Boot boots cleanly (RP1 init, PCIe link up, eth0 detected), but it stops at the **U-Boot autoboot prompt** (`U-Boot> [B`) rather than proceeding to boot the kernel. No GRUB, no kernel console output at all — this is earlier than where the previous CM5 failure was (which at least got past GRUB before going silent).

A few things stand out:
1. This is a **Pi 5**, not CM5 (`RPI 5 Model B (0xd04170)`) — different SKU than what was tested for the netconsole fix.
2. `/cmdline.txt not found` and `Failed to open command line file` — that could be benign (RPi firmware looking for a legacy file that Talos doesn't use) or could indicate something didn't get written to the SD card correctly.
3. It's sitting at an **interactive U-Boot prompt** — autoboot was interrupted somehow ("Hit any key to stop autoboot: 0" followed by immediately dropping to prompt), which suggests either a keypress was sent (e.g., from the terminal/JetKVM) or autoboot itself isn't proceeding.

Let me check if there's more recent scrollback — this could be stale from an earlier boot attempt, not necessarily the current "stuck" state.

Same content — this is genuinely the current, static state: the board is parked at an interactive `U-Boot>` prompt, autoboot did not proceed. Notably, `Out: serial,vidconsole` / `Err: serial,vidconsole` — U-Boot's own output is going to serial (which we're seeing) *and* HDMI, but that's separate from the Linux kernel console.

A few real hypotheses, not guesses to act on blindly:

1. **`/cmdline.txt not found`** is likely a red herring — Talos images typically don't use RPi's legacy `cmdline.txt` firmware convention; U-Boot itself has its own boot script/environment. Worth confirming against a known-good v1.13.6 image if you have one, but probably not the cause.
2. **Autoboot didn't fire** — "Hit any key to stop autoboot: 0" then immediately `U-Boot>` suggests either (a) something in the environment/boot script caused U-Boot to abort into the interactive shell rather than genuinely being interrupted by a keypress, or (b) the boot script/extlinux.conf on the SD card's boot partition is missing, malformed, or not being found.
3. This is **before** the kernel is even reached — so this is not the same failure as the CM5 netconsole issue (that got past U-Boot/GRUB and into kernel boot, then went silent). This looks like a U-Boot-level boot-script problem, possibly specific to Pi 5 vs CM5, or specific to this SD card image/flash.

Let's check what's actually on the boot partition to see if the boot script exists.

Good on both fronts: the release pipeline finished successfully (all three workflows: `success`), and now we have a clearer picture on the boot issue too.

So `run bootcmd` **did** work — it reached the GRUB menu and offered `Talos v1.13.8`. The autoboot appeared stuck earlier probably because it was just sitting at the menu countdown/timeout waiting for input, not actually broken (or the earlier scrollback was mid-transition). The real failure is: **selecting the Talos v1.13.8 entry reboots the board instead of booting the kernel** — this is now clearly downstream of GRUB, at or near kernel handoff. That's the same territory as the CM5 silent-reboot bug `ad30ca4` addressed, just now confirmed on Pi 5 too, and apparently *still happening* even after netconsole was removed.

Let's capture what's on screen right at the moment of reboot.

This scrollback shows the board has already reset — it's back at the very beginning of firmware boot (`Starting OS...`, `U-Boot 2026.01...`), confirming your report: selecting the Talos entry from GRUB causes a hard reset back to power-on, not a graceful kernel panic/hang. That's consistent with `ad30ca4`'s hypothesis of a very early crash before any console output flushes — except this is happening **without netconsole** in the image now, so the earlier root-cause theory (netconsole/macb interaction) is likely wrong, or incomplete.

Since `console=ttyAMA0,115200` should still be active and this is a hard reset with zero kernel-side output even via UART, the failure is happening extremely early — likely before the kernel's console subsystem initializes, or it's a firmware/EFI-stub/GRUB-to-kernel handoff problem specific to this hardware combination (real Pi 5, not CM5 — worth noting the bug report `ad30ca4` was based on was CM5-specific hardware).

At the GRUB menu, press `e` to edit the `Talos v1.13.8` entry. You'll see its kernel command line (likely something with `linux`, a path to the kernel image, and args including `console=ttyAMA0,115200` plus Talos's own defaults).

A few things to try/capture:
1. First just paste back what the edit screen shows as-is (the full `linux ...` and `initrd ...` lines) — that tells us exactly what GRUB is about to pass to the kernel.
2. Then, if you're comfortable editing it, try adding `earlycon=pl011,mmio32,0x107d001000` (BCM2712's UART10/debug-UART MMIO base — this gets us kernel output *before* the normal console driver initializes, which `console=ttyAMA0` alone doesn't guarantee) right after `console=ttyAMA0,115200`, then boot with Ctrl+X or F10.

Let's start with just reading the entry first — paste back what you see.

``` │setparams 'A - Talos v1.13.8-rpi'                                                                        │  │                                                                                                         │
 │  set gfxmode=auto                                                                                       │  │  set gfxpayload=text                                                                                    │
 │  linux /A/vmlinuz talos.platform=metal console=tty0 console=ttyAMA0,115200 console=ttyAMA10,115200 sysc\│  │tl.kernel.kexec_load_disabled=1 talos.dashboard.disabled=1 init_on_alloc=1 slab_nomerge pti=on consolebl\│
 │ank=0 nvme_core.io_timeout=4294967295 printk.devkmsg=on selinux=1 module.sig_enforce=1 proc_mem.force_ov\│
 │erride=never                                                                                             │
 │  initrd /A/initramfs.xz                                                                                 │  │``` is the grub config

Very informative. The kernel cmdline has `console=ttyAMA0,115200 console=ttyAMA10,115200` — **two different `ttyAMA` consoles**, and `ttyAMA10` is new information. Recall CLAUDE.md's earlier UART investigation confirmed *"uart10 (the JST-SH debug UART) is the only PL011 instance enabled in the BCM2712 DT, so it still registers as ttyAMA0."* But this cmdline explicitly names `ttyAMA10` too — meaning something (Talos's `DefaultArgs()` or the imager) is adding a *second* console pointing at a device node that may not exist or may conflict with `ttyAMA0`.

This is worth checking directly rather than guessing — where does `console=ttyAMA10,115200` come from, since it's not something this repo's Makefile sets (only `console=ttyAMA0,115200` is in `EXTRA_KERNEL_ARGS`).

content.text:
Confirmed — this repo only ever sets `console=ttyAMA0,115200`. `console=ttyAMA10,115200` isn't coming from anything in this codebase — it must be coming from Talos's own imager `DefaultArgs()`/upstream defaults, or possibly from the overlay's own boot config. Also worth noting: `console=tty0` is there too (three consoles total), which is standard Talos default (HDMI/video console) — that one's normal and not Pi-specific.

The theory now: if `ttyAMA10` doesn't correspond to a valid device on this DT (recall CLAUDE.md's own notes say only one PL011 instance is enabled, registering as `ttyAMA0`), the kernel could be panicking very early trying to initialize a console on a non-existent/misconfigured UART — and a kernel panic with `panic_on_oops` or similar could trigger a hard reset via the watchdog before anything reaches the working `ttyAMA0`.

  - **Ctrl+E** — jump to end of line

Simplest approach: use arrow keys to position the cursor right after `console=ttyAMA10,115200 ` (right before `systcl.kernel.kexec_load_disabled=1`), then press **Backspace** repeatedly (25 times — `console=ttyAMA10,115200 ` is 24 chars + the space) to remove exactly that substring, leaving `ttyAMA0` and everything else intact.

GRUB's edit screen reformats/wraps the line for display — every time you move around or the screen redraws, it can look like your edit "reverted" even if the underlying text changed, because line-wrap boundaries shift as text gets shorter. It's easy to mistake a wrap-redraw for a revert.

A more reliable way to check without guessing: after editing, move the cursor with **Ctrl+E** to jump to the true end of that logical line — if your edit actually stuck, the line will be shorter and `proc_mem.force_override=never` (the last arg) should now appear sooner. Let's see it.

This is a real signal, and it's not from the kernel — this is **U-Boot's own USB stack** (still in firmware, not Talos), spamming `Resetting EP 2... WARN endpoint is halted` in a tight loop, forever. Endpoint 2 on a USB controller repeatedly halting and resetting is exactly the XHCI keyboard-detection issue we saw earlier in the scrollback (`Failed to get keyboard state from device 1d6b:0104`, `Bus usb@200000: 1 USB Device(s) found`) — this is U-Boot polling a USB device (likely the JetKVM's own USB-HID emulation, or a hub) whose endpoint 2 won't stay up, and getting stuck retrying indefinitely.

This is a completely different and important finding: **U-Boot itself may be hanging/looping on USB enumeration**, separate from anything Talos-side. This could even be what's *causing* the apparent "crash and reboot" — if U-Boot's USB polling loop never returns, the watchdog could be firing and resetting the board, which would look exactly like what you've been seeing (silent reset, back to power-on).

RPi5 is now in it's expected reboot loop again

So even with USB disconnected, the reboot loop persists — that rules out the USB EP2 hang as the root cause too. It was a real symptom, but not causal. Let's look at the fresh scrollback now to see the current state and whether the EP2 spam is gone (confirming USB really is out of the picture) and what happens after it.

Important new detail: `DEV [01:00] 2.00 000000:02 class 0 VID 1d6b PID 0104` / `MSD device...register MSD` — **VID 1d6b is the Linux Foundation's generic USB gadget vendor ID**, and this is registering as a **Mass Storage Device (MSD)**, not a keyboard. So the thing plugged into USB and causing EP2 to halt is actually JetKVM's own **USB mass-storage/virtual-media gadget** (JetKVM emulates a USB drive for ISO/image mounting), not a keyboard as I assumed earlier — and evidently it's still connected/detected even after your unplug attempt, or this is a fresh boot where it got replugged.

But more importantly: this fresh trace confirms the loop is a firmware-level SD card boot sequence (GPT read, FAT32, DTB load, "Starting OS") — completely deterministic and identical every time, ending at `Starting the controller / USB XHCI 1.10` — right where the EP2 spam would begin. This is firmware behavior, not something Talos or the kernel controls.

input.prompt:
I need current, up-to-date research (no code changes) on Talos Linux's official/upstream support for Raspberry Pi 5 and CM4/CM5, as of now (mid-August 2026). This is to help decide whether a heavily-patched custom fork (github.com/conallob/talos-rpi-builder, which forks siderolabs/sbc-raspberrypi at an unmerged PR #88 branch to get unified rpi_generic BCM2711/BCM2712 support) is still necessary, or whether stock Talos + factory.talos.dev can now handle Pi 5/CM5 out of the box.

Context on what this fork exists for (as of its last check, per its own CLAUDE.md docs):
- siderolabs/sbc-raspberrypi#88 (unifying BCM2711/BCM2712 into one rpi_generic overlay, by @appkins) was still open/unmerged as of mid-July 2026. Maintainer @frezbo wants to keep rpi_5 as a separate overlay for factory.talos.dev/Image Factory compatibility, and on 2026-07-17 added a new blocker asking to confirm the patches are already upstreamed elsewhere before merging. @appkins said his own U-Boot fork diverged too far from PR #88 to easily reconcile.
- A macb/PCIe-ethernet TX-stall bug (siderolabs/sbc-raspberrypi#82, #91) had a fix land in siderolabs/pkgs main (PR #1526, merged ~2026-04-29) but field reports as of mid-May 2026 said it only mitigates, not fully eliminates, the stall.
- A separate sdio1 broken-cd DTB issue causes endless "mmc0: Timeout waiting for hardware cmd interrupt" polling on CM5 when boot is NVMe-only — fixed locally via a carried patch, not verified upstream.
- The Talos umbrella tracking issue (siderolabs/talos#12748) was auto-closed back in Feb 2026, seemingly resolved via sbc-raspberrypi v0.1.9 + an updated imager overlay tag per maintainer dsseng — but the underlying PR #88 unification work was NOT part of that resolution, it stayed separate.

Please check, as of right now:
1. Status of siderolabs/sbc-raspberrypi#88 — merged, closed, still open? Any resolution?
2. Whether factory.talos.dev (Image Factory) now offers a working Raspberry Pi 5 or CM5 image/overlay selection, and whether users report it actually boots successfully on real Pi 5/CM5 hardware (check recent GitHub issues, Talos community Slack/Discord discussion if surfaced via search, siderolabs/talos issues, or the Talos docs' SBC/Raspberry Pi support page).
3. Whether there's a newer/different official overlay version (e.g. sbc-raspberrypi v0.1.10+, or something following v0.1.9) with better Pi5/CM5 support than what existed in Feb 2026.
4. Any newly reported issues specifically about Pi 5 boards failing to boot Talos with a hard reset/reboot loop right around kernel handoff (GRUB → kernel), especially anything involving USB XHCI endpoint stalls during U-Boot boot on Pi 5 — this might be a known issue with a fix, or an EEPROM/bootloader firmware version problem.
5. Any changes to the recommended Raspberry Pi bootloader EEPROM version requirements for Talos on Pi5/CM5.

Report back concisely (bullet points, under 400 words): what's changed since mid-July 2026, and specifically whether switching to stock Talos + factory.talos.dev for Pi5/CM5 is now a viable, simpler alternative to this custom fork. If nothing has changed, say so plainly.

content.text:
That's a clear answer, and it actually validates the fork's continued existence rather than undermining it. Summary:

**Stock Talos + factory.talos.dev is not currently viable for Pi 5/CM5.** The picture is worse than we thought, not better:

Now we can see the real, meaningful upstream diff on `cm5.dtsi`:
1. `pinctrl-names`/`pinctrl-0 = <&eth0_irq_pins>` **added**
2. `phy1: ethernet-phy@1` → `ethernet-phy@0` (address changed **0x1 → 0x0**)

This is exactly what the v0.2.1 research summary described. Now — critically — our own patch's header comment explicitly says: *"BCM54213PE on CM5 Rev 1.0 CMIO4 strapped to MDIO addr 1"* and that our patch **reverts** phy addr `@0/0x0` back to `@1/0x1` because our hardware needs address 1, not 0. Let's look at our full patch to see exactly what it does to the CM5 section.

Now the picture is fully clear. This patch is a **reverse patch**: it takes upstream's already-correct DTS/DTSI (with `mdio{}` wrapper, `interrupt-parent = <&rp1_gpio>`, `pinctrl-0`) and applies PR #88's *old broken* transformation on top, then hand-corrects the PHY address back to `@1` for CM5 hardware specifically. Wait — re-reading the header comment again: this patch's `-` lines (removed) are the flat structure, `+` lines (added) are the `mdio{}` wrapper. That means **this patch converts the correct upstream structure INTO the broken `mdio{}` structure** that `build-overlay.yml`'s own comment says breaks the vendor RP1 driver.

This is the crux of it. Both old and new DTB sources have flat structure (no `mdio{}` wrapper) — so deleting PR #88's broken `0008` and applying nothing else is directionally correct for both. **But the PHY address differs between old and new**: old = `phy1: ethernet-phy@1` (`reg=<0x1>`), new = `phy1: ethernet-phy@0` (`reg=<0x0>`).

This is exactly the detail our orphaned patch's header comment flagged: *"BCM54213PE on CM5 Rev 1.0 CMIO4 strapped to MDIO addr 1"* — meaning the actual CM5 hardware's ethernet PHY is wired to answer at MDIO address **1**, not 0. If we bump to `stable_20260724` as-is (with `ethernet-phy@0`, `reg=<0x0>`), **that would break ethernet on real CM5 hardware** unless something else compensates.

questions.question: stable_20260724's cm5.dtsi has the PHY at address 0 (ethernet-phy@0, reg=<0x0>), but our repo's orphaned patch comment says real CM5 hardware (BCM54213PE, Rev 1.0 CMIO4) is strapped to MDIO address 1 — and that patch was never actually wired into the build. From: Stephen Wheet <stephen@wheet>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 00:00:00 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] ARM: dts: bcm2712-rpi-cm5: Trust hardware card-detect on sdio1

The BCM2712 SDHCI controller exposes a working SDHCI_CARD_PRESENT bit
in its PRESENT_STATE register and raises SDHCI_INT_CARD_INSERT/REMOVE
on physical state changes. On carriers that route the microSD slot's
card-detect line to the controller's native CD pin (CM4IO, CM5IO,
DeskPi Super6C, and the upstream RPi CM4/CM5 IO board reference
designs), broken-cd is unnecessary.

With broken-cd set, drivers/mmc/core/host.c sets MMC_CAP_NEEDS_POLL,
which prevents mmc_rescan() from short-circuiting when the slot is
empty. The kernel then issues CMD52 (SDIO probe) into the empty slot,
which never completes, and sdhci_timeout_timer() emits

  mmc0: Timeout waiting for hardware cmd interrupt.
  ============ SDHCI REGISTER DUMP ===========

every ~10 seconds for the lifetime of the system.

Drop broken-cd. The controller's native card-detect handles both
empty-slot quiet and hot-insert via SDHCI_INT_CARD_INSERT.

CARRIER COMPATIBILITY: This change assumes the carrier wires microSD
CD to the BCM2712 native CD pin. Verified on: CM4IO, CM5IO, DeskPi
Super6C. Carriers that route CD to a GPIO instead must use

The README's own check (`sudo rpi-eeprom-update`) requires booting a working OS, which is circular here since Talos can't boot to run it. But the boot log line itself — `RPi: BOOTSYS release VERSION:8124798b DATE: 2026/02/06` — is the definitive, direct answer to your question:

**Your CM5's EEPROM/bootloader firmware build date is 2026-02-06.** That's well after "late 2024" (the README's cited cutoff for NVMe/PCIe boot support), so it's not the *stale, pre-2024* firmware the README warns about.

That said, a few caveats worth being upfront about:
- This confirms the firmware is *recent*, not that it's the *literal latest* release — there's no way to diff against "latest" from the boot log alone; that requires `rpi-eeprom-update` from a booted OS or checking the [`raspberrypi/rpi-eeprom`](https://github.com/raspberrypi/rpi-eeprom) release list against `8124798b`.
- You're booting from **SD card**, not NVMe — the README's EEPROM warning is specifically about NVMe/PCIe enumeration in U-Boot. Since this board is on SD, that particular EEPROM dependency likely isn't the cause of this hang.
- The hang itself happens **after** U-Boot/GRUB successfully load and select the kernel, well past the point where stale-EEPROM failures typically manifest (those usually show as boot device enumeration failures earlier in the log, or hangs at the U-Boot splash — not a clean GRUB menu → silent reset).

So: EEPROM is recent, and given you're on SD (not NVMe) the classic EEPROM failure mode doesn't fit this symptom anyway. I'd lean toward this not being an EEPROM issue, but I don't want to assert that as settled — want me to note the exact `8124798b` build against the raspberrypi/rpi-eeprom release history to double check, or move on to a different hypothesis for the hang?

172	Assembles the disk image and upgrade installer using the pre-built kernel and overlay from Steps 1 and 2. **Do not run this until both prior steps have completed successfully and `CUSTOM_INSTALLER_BASE` / `CUSTOM_OVERLAY_IMAGE` in the Makefile point to the correct tags.**
173	
174	**Triggers:**
175	- Push a version tag (e.g. `git tag v1.13.8 && git push --tags`) → full build + publish
176	- Manual run via **Actions → Build and Publish → Run workflow**
177	
178	**Workflow dispatch inputs:**
179	
180	| Input | Default | Description |
181	|-------|---------|-------------|
182	| `talos_version` | _(from Makefile)_ | Override Talos version |
183	| `extra_kernel_args` | _(empty)_ | Space-separated `key=value` kernel args (e.g. `cma=256M hugepages=64`) |
184	| `extra_extensions` | _(empty)_ | Extra extension image refs on top of the two defaults |
185	
186	**Pipeline jobs:**
187	1. **`resolve-version`** — resolves Talos version, reads `CUSTOM_INSTALLER_BASE` and `CUSTOM_OVERLAY_IMAGE` from Makefile; forwards `extra_kernel_args` and `extra_extensions`
188	2. **`build`** — resolves extension images to digests via `crane digest` for reproducible builds, then:
189	   - Builds disk image (`make build`)
190	   - Builds installer OCI (`make installer`)
191	   - Pushes installer to GHCR tagged `:vX.Y.Z`
192	   - Uploads `metal-arm64.raw.xz` as artifact
193	3. **`release`** — downloads artifact and creates the GitHub release
194	
195	---
196	
197	## Prerequisites (local builds only)
198	
199	- **Podman** or **Docker** (with privileged container support)
200	- **macOS** or **Linux** host (arm64 recommended for U-Boot build)
201	- `make`
202	- `gh` CLI for publishing: `brew install gh && gh auth login`
203	
204	---
205	
206	## Quick Start
207	
208	### Download a release
209	
210	Download from the [Releases page](https://github.com/wheetazlab/talos-rpi-builder/releases):
211	
212	| File | For |
213	|------|-----|
214	| `metal-arm64.raw.xz` | CM4, CM5, Pi 4, Pi 5 (all variants) |
215	
216	### Flash to SD card / eMMC
217	
218	```bash
219	# macOS
220	xzcat metal-arm64.raw.xz | sudo dd of=/dev/rdiskN bs=4m
221	
222	# Linux
223	xzcat metal-arm64.raw.xz | sudo dd of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress
224	```
225	
226	Or with make (after building locally):
227	```bash
228	make flash-sd DISK=/dev/rdisk4
229	```
230	
231	### eMMC via rpiboot
232	
233	1. Set the CM5 into USB boot mode (check your carrier board manual for the jumper/button)
234	2. Connect via USB-C and run `sudo rpiboot`
235	3. Flash to the exposed eMMC disk
236	
237	
238	---
239	
240	## Local Build
241	
242	### Prerequisites: build overlay first
243	
244	`make build` pulls `rpi-talos` and `sbc-raspberrypi` from GHCR. The kernel installer-base is built in CI (`build-kernel.yml`) — there is no local-build script for it. The overlay does have a local script:
245	
246	```bash
247	# Build sbc-raspberrypi overlay → ghcr.io/<org>/sbc-raspberrypi:pr88-cd5
248	./scripts/build-overlay.sh
249	```
250	
251	The script requires:
252	- Docker or Podman **logged in** to GHCR (`docker login ghcr.io -u <user>`)
253	- `crane` installed (`brew install crane` or `go install github.com/google/go-containerregistry/cmd/crane@latest`)
254	
255	Override defaults with env vars or flags:
256	
257	```bash
258	# build-overlay.sh options
259	GHCR_ORG=myorg OVERLAY_TAG=pr88 ./scripts/build-overlay.sh
260	
261	# pin overlay internals for CM5
262	GHCR_ORG=myorg OVERLAY_TAG=pr88-cm5 \
263	UBOOT_VERSION=2026.01 \
264	UBOOT_SHA256=b60d5865cefdbc75da8da4156c56c458e00de75a49b80c1a2e58a96e30ad0d54 \
265	RPI_DTB_REF=stable_20260724 \
266	./scripts/build-overlay.sh
267	
268	./scripts/build-overlay.sh --help
269	```
270	
271	`build-overlay.sh` overrides affect only the `sbc-raspberrypi` overlay (U-Boot + DTBs). They do **not** switch Talos to a different kernel.
272	
273	`UBOOT_VERSION`/`UBOOT_SHA*` refer to upstream `u-boot/u-boot` source tarballs (`u-boot-<ver>.tar.bz2` from `ftp.denx.de`), not prebuilt image checksums.
274	
275	### Build disk image (after kernel+overlay are in GHCR)
276	
277	```bash
278	# Full pipeline (build image + installer + push + release)
279	make publish
280	
281	# Individual steps
282	make build        # Talos disk image → _out/metal-arm64.raw.xz
283	make installer    # Installer OCI   → _out/installer-arm64.tar
284	make release      # GitHub release with .raw.xz artifact
285	```
286	
287	---
288	
289	## Customization
290	
291	```bash
292	# Different Talos version
293	make build TALOS_VERSION=v1.13.8
294	
295	# Override overlay image
296	make build CUSTOM_OVERLAY_IMAGE=ghcr.io/conallob/sbc-raspberrypi:pr88-cd5
297	
298	# Extra kernel args
299	make build EXTRA_KERNEL_ARGS='--extra-kernel-arg=cma=256M --extra-kernel-arg=hugepages=64'
300	```
301	
302	### Custom extensions
303	
304	Override the full extension set (replaces defaults):
305	
306	```bash
307	make build EXTENSIONS="ghcr.io/siderolabs/iscsi-tools:v0.2.0 ghcr.io/siderolabs/util-linux-tools:2.41.4 ghcr.io/siderolabs/gvisor:20260202.0"
308	```
309	
310	Browse available extensions: https://github.com/siderolabs/extensions
311	
312	### Via workflow dispatch (CI)
313	
314	`publish.yml` exposes `extra_kernel_args` and `extra_extensions` as workflow inputs. Extension images are resolved to digests (`image@sha256:...`) before the build for reproducibility.
315	
316	---
317	
318	## Build Targets
319	
320	```
321	make build          Build the raw disk image
322	make installer      Build the Talos installer image (for talosctl upgrade)
323	make publish        Full pipeline: build → installer → push → release
324	make flash-sd       Flash image to disk (requires DISK=/dev/rdiskN)
325	make pull-images    Pre-pull all required container images
326	make clean          Remove _out/ directory
327	make help           Show all targets and version variables
328	```
329	
330	---
331	
332	### What's in the image?
333	
334	- Talos Linux kernel + initramfs (arm64) — from `ghcr.io/conallob/rpi-talos:v1.13.8-k-rpi` (`raspberrypi/linux` rpi-6.18.y vendor fork, built by `build-kernel.yml`)
335	- **Patched U-Boot** (BCM2712/RP1) from `ghcr.io/conallob/sbc-raspberrypi:pr88-cd5` (PR #88 patch set — NVMe/PCIe, EEE LPI, MACB driver)
336	- DTBs from custom `sbc-raspberrypi` overlay (`rpi_generic` installer):
337	  - `bcm2711-rpi-4-b.dtb` ← Pi 4 Model B
338	  - `bcm2711-rpi-cm4.dtb` ← CM4 (CM4IO and compatible carriers)
339	  - `bcm2712-rpi-cm5-cm4io.dtb` ← CM4IO-compatible carriers (e.g. DeskPi Super6C)
340	  - `bcm2712-rpi-cm5-cm5io.dtb`
341	  - `bcm2712-rpi-cm5l-cm4io.dtb`
342	  - `bcm2712-rpi-cm5l-cm5io.dtb`
343	  - `bcm2712-rpi-5-b.dtb`
344	  - `bcm2712d0-rpi-5-b.dtb`
345	- System extension: `iscsi-tools v0.2.0`
346	- System extension: `util-linux-tools 2.41.4`
347	- Kernel arg: _(none — single image supports all CM4/CM5/Pi 4/Pi 5 variants)
348	
349	---
350	
351	## After Booting
352	
353	Talos enters **maintenance mode** waiting for a machine config:
354	
355	```bash
356	# Generate config
357	talosctl gen config my-cluster https://<CONTROLPLANE_IP>:6443 \
358	  --additional-sans <CONTROLPLANE_IP>
359	
360	# Apply to node
361	talosctl apply-config --insecure --nodes <NODE_IP> --file controlplane.yaml \
362	  --talosconfig talosconfig
363	
364	# Bootstrap etcd (first control-plane node only)
365	talosctl bootstrap --nodes <CONTROLPLANE_IP> --talosconfig talosconfig
366	
367	# Get kubeconfig
368	talosctl kubeconfig --nodes <CONTROLPLANE_IP> --talosconfig talosconfig
369	```
370	
371	To upgrade an existing node:
372	
373	```bash
374	talosctl upgrade --nodes <NODE_IP> --image ghcr.io/conallob/talos-rpi-installer:v1.13.8
375	```

name: project-cm4-cluster-pivot

As of 2026-09-03, the plan is to build the actual Talos cluster on **CM4** hardware rather than waiting on CM5/Pi5:
- 1x CM4 with WiFi + Bluetooth as the control-plane node
- 6x CM4 as a worker nodepool

**How to apply:** CM4 (BCM2711) is already fully supported by the existing unified `rpi_generic` image built by [[talos-rpi-builder-overview]] — no repo/build changes are needed for the CM4 cluster pivot; this is purely a deployment/cluster-config task (talosctl gen config, applying to 7 physical nodes, bootstrap). Continue treating CM5/Pi5 boot-loop debugging as separate, lower-priority follow-up work — don't block cluster standup on it. name: Build RPi-Kernel Installer Base

# Builds the installer-base OCI image used by publish.yml, with the
# Raspberry Pi vendor kernel (raspberrypi/linux rpi-6.18.y) instead of
# the upstream stable kernel.
#
# The kernel package itself is built by the reusable build-kernel-pkg.yml
# workflow and tagged by content hash, so reruns that don't touch the
# kernel config / pkgs patch / linux_ref skip the kernel rebuild and
# reuse the published image.
#
# Output: ghcr.io/<owner>/rpi-talos:<installer_tag>
#   default tag: v1.13.8-k-rpi
#
# Trigger:
#   - workflow_dispatch  (manual)
#   - push of a tag matching v*-kernel  (e.g. v1.13.8-kernel)
#   - a GitHub Release being published (e.g. via scripts/release.sh) —
#     uses the release's tag_name as talos_version, same defaults as a
#     v*-kernel tag push otherwise.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      talos_version:
        description: 'Talos version (e.g. v1.13.8)'
        required: false
        default: 'v1.13.8'
      pkg_version:
        description: 'siderolabs/pkgs ref — must match the base of the vendored Pkgfile patch (anchored on tag v1.13.0)'
        required: false
        default: 'v1.13.0'
      linux_ref:
        description: 'raspberrypi/linux short SHA pinned by the vendored Pkgfile patch — workflow asserts the vendored patch matches'
        required: false
        default: '79dc190b12f9'
      installer_tag:
        description: 'Output image tag (e.g. v1.13.8-k-rpi)'
        required: false
        default: 'v1.13.8-k-rpi'
      kernel_image:
        description: 'Optional: fully-qualified kernel image ref to use (e.g. ghcr.io/me/kernel-rpi:my-tag). If set, skips both cache lookup and kernel rebuild.'
        required: false
        default: ''
      force_rebuild_kernel:
        description: 'Force a kernel rebuild even if the content-hashed kernel image is already published'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      runner:
        description: 'GitHub Actions runner (e.g. ubuntu-24.04-arm, mac-runner)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04-arm'
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*-kernel'
  release:
    types: [published]

## [Talos 1.14.0](https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/releases/tag/v1.14.0) (2026-09-03)

Welcome to the v1.14.0 release of Talos!



Please try out the release binaries and report any issues at
https://github.com/siderolabs/talos/issues.

### DNS over TLS (DoT) and DNS over HTTPS (DoH) Support

Talos now supports DNS over TLS (DoT) and DNS over HTTPS (DoH) for secure DNS resolution.
These features allow Talos to encrypt DNS queries and responses, enhancing privacy and security for DNS traffic.
The DNS protocol can be configured on a per-name server basis in the `ResolverConfig` document, allowing for flexible configuration of DNS resolution.


### Apply Configuration Modes

The '--mode=reboot' option has been removed from the `talosctl apply-config` command; by default, configuration is applied without a reboot.
Most configuration changes don't require a reboot; the documentation lists the changes that do.


### Native BGP

Talos now supports running native BGP routing instances on the host via embedded GoBGP servers, configured with `BGPInstanceConfig` documents.
This removes the need to ship FRR as a system extension for the common fabric-facing use case.

List of changes:

- Added repeatable, named `BGPInstanceConfig` documents to configure local ASN, router-id, optional Linux VRF, advertised interfaces, neighbors, and per-route preferred source (`routeSource`).
- Peer hold-time and BFD behavior are configured inline on each concrete neighbor, which selects either an address or a link.
- Numbered and unnumbered (IPv6 link-local, RFC 8950 extended next-hop) peering are supported, including IPv4 prefixes learned over an IPv6 link-local next-hop.
- Neighbor-local ASN overrides and passive sessions are supported. ECMP (multipath) and BFD (fast failure detection) are supported for fabric peering.
- BFD is currently supported only by the instance in the default routing domain; GoBGP's embedded BFD listener is not VRF-aware.
- Each instance owns an isolated BGP RIB and, by default, installs learned routes into its default or VRF routing table through the existing route controllers. Set `installRoutes: false` to retain learned routes in the BGP RIB without installing them into the Linux routing table.
- Instances can selectively import best neighbor-learned routes from other named instances with `importRoutes` prefix selectors. Imports are one-way, preserve path attributes, and do not recursively import locally originated or previously imported paths.
- Peer state is observable via instance-qualified `BGPPeerStatus` resources (`talosctl get bgppeerstatus`).
- `RouteSpec`/`RouteStatus` now carry a multipath next-hop list to support ECMP and cross-family (RFC 8950) next-hops.


### Btrfs Support

Talos now supports mounting and provisioning `btrfs` filesystem for user volumes and existing volumes.

Support for `btrfs` is enabled by installing `btrfs` system extension.


### Unified --namespace Flag

`talosctl containers`, `logs`, `stats` and `restart` now select the containerd namespace through the same `--namespace` flag and vocabulary already used by `talosctl image` and `talosctl debug`: `system` (the default), `cri` for Kubernetes workloads, and `taloscontainers` for containers declared via a `ContainerConfig` document.

The `--kubernetes`/`-k` flag is deprecated in favor of `--namespace cri`.

`talosctl image list` also supports `--namespace taloscontainers`, to inspect images pulled for `ContainerConfig` containers. `talosctl debug` does not support the `taloscontainers` namespace.


### CRI Base Runtime Specification Configuration

Talos now supports overriding the default OCI runtime specification for CRI containers with a
`CRIBaseRuntimeSpecConfig` document:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1alpha1
kind: CRIBaseRuntimeSpecConfig
overrides:
  process:
    rlimits:
      - type: RLIMIT_NOFILE
        hard: 1024
        soft: 1024
```

The `.machine.baseRuntimeSpecOverrides` field is deprecated and remains supported during the deprecation
period. It is mutually exclusive with `CRIBaseRuntimeSpecConfig`; configurations containing both are rejected.

Applying, updating, or removing either source regenerates the base runtime specification and restarts CRI
automatically. A machine reboot is no longer required.


### CRI Customization Configuration

Talos now supports customizing the CRI containerd configuration with named `CRICustomizationConfig`
documents. Each document contains a TOML fragment; fragments are merged in lexicographical order by name.
Applying, updating, or removing these documents updates the generated CRI configuration and restarts CRI
automatically.

The legacy `/etc/cri/conf.d/20-customization.part` machine-file configuration remains supported during the
deprecation period and is exposed under the reserved name `customization`. A `CRICustomizationConfig` document
cannot use that name.

NOTE: a machine reboot is no longer required to apply changes to CRI configuration.


### Containerd NRI

Talos no longer disables NRI (Node Resource Interface) for the CRI containerd instance by default, so NRI is available
to use without any machine config patches.

To bring back the old behavior of NRI disabled by default, add the following machine configuration document:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1alpha1
kind: CRICustomizationConfig
name: disable-nri
content: |
  [plugins]
    [plugins."io.containerd.nri.v1.nri"]
       disable = true
```

content.text:
This is genuinely relevant — upstream `siderolabs/pkgs` has been actively landing BCM2712/RP1 fixes since the base this repo's patch was cut against. Notably:

- `fix: bring in a change to BCM2712_MIP` and `fix: enable CONFIG_BCM2712_MIP as built-in` — a Pi 5/CM5-specific kernel config option
- `fix: macb silent TX stall on BCM2712/RP1` (multiple rounds — RFC then v2 netdev patches) — this is the exact same macb TX-stall issue this repo's CLAUDE.md already tracks as "fixed upstream in raspberrypi/linux at the pinned linux_ref"
- `fix: backport macb IEEE 802.3az EEE support for Raspberry Pi 5 RP1`

But — critically — **this repo doesn't consume `siderolabs/pkgs`' kernel at all for the Pi build**. Per CLAUDE.md, it swaps in `raspberrypi/linux` rpi-6.18.y via the `0001-Patched-for-Raspberry-Pi-5.patch`, precisely because the vendor fork already carries these fixes ahead of upstream. So these upstream `pkgs` improvements don't directly help unless `pkg_version` is bumped — which CLAUDE.md says not to do casually, and which isn't tagged yet anyway (`pkgs` has no tag past `v1.13.0`, confirmed above — these commits aren't in a release yet).

None of this looks like it touches the actual **U-Boot/DTB/overlay boot hang** you're chasing (GRUB→kernel silent reset) — that's an `sbc-raspberrypi`/overlay-layer issue, not a Talos or pkgs kernel-module issue.

**Short answer: no, v1.14.0 itself doesn't contain a fix for the CM5/Pi5 boot-loop.** The only CM5/Pi5-relevant activity is in `pkgs`' kernel-config/patch history (BCM2712_MIP config, macb EEE/TX-stall), which this repo bypasses via the vendor kernel anyway, and which isn't in a tagged `pkgs` release regardless. This doesn't change the CM4 pivot plan — continuing with the v1.14.0 Talos bump for the CM4 cluster now.

Two independent trimmed modules have dangling symbol dependencies against our reduced module set:

1. **`hibmc-drm.ko`** needs `i2c_bit_add_bus` — from `i2c-algo-bit.ko`
2. **`panfrost.ko`** needs a dozen `drm_sched_*` symbols — from `gpu-sched.ko` (DRM scheduler core)

Neither symbol provider is in our trimmed `hack/modules-arm64.txt`. Both `hibmc-drm` and `panfrost` are themselves almost certainly irrelevant to CM4/CM5/Pi4/Pi5 hardware (HiSilicon BMC display, Mali/Panfrost GPU — Pi doesn't use either of these DRM drivers; RPi uses `vc4`/`v3d`). The cleanest fix is to drop `hibmc-drm.ko` and `panfrost.ko` themselves from the module list, rather than pulling in their dependency chains for modules we'll never load.
